headline: Chip-led Nasdaq selloff and a Hormuz LNG strike pushed bond yields higher on Tuesday; FOMC minutes this afternoon are the day's decisive catalyst.
stance: Cautious/Rotational. Tuesday's cash close showed the S&P 500 (PRIOR CASH CLOSE 7,503.85) holding while the Nasdaq 100 (PRIOR CASH CLOSE 25,818.69) dropped ~1.8% as semiconductors were hit; breadth on the NYSE was nearly flat, signalling rotation rather than outright liquidation. The 10-year Treasury yield (OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET ~4.56%) is creeping higher on renewed Hormuz-security fears and hawkish Fed pricing — that is the single biggest headwind to expensive growth stocks today. Positioning is a tailwind: futures speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Nasdaq 100 and Russell 2000 — a contrarian floor — but copper speculators are heavily positioned long at the 95th percentile, a contrarian warning for industrial-metals bulls.

news.head: Semiconductor rout
news.body: A gauge of chip stocks fell more than 4.5% on Tuesday on fears that massive AI capital spending may not justify current valuations, dragging the Nasdaq 100 down ~1.8% at the cash close.

news.head: SpaceX joins Nasdaq 100
news.body: SpaceX (SPCX) officially entered the Nasdaq 100 on Jul 7 under new fast-track IPO rules, becoming the first $2-trillion-market-cap addition via that pathway.

news.head: Hormuz LNG strike
news.body: A Qatari LNG carrier was struck by a projectile while exiting the Strait of Hormuz, reigniting Middle East security fears and pushing WTI crude sharply higher overnight.

news.head: FOMC minutes due today
news.body: The Fed releases minutes from its June 16-17 meeting this afternoon; the dot-plot already shows nine of 18 officials penciling in at least one rate hike by year-end, so any hawkish language could move bonds and equities immediately.

news.head: June payrolls miss lingers
news.body: Last week's 57,000 June nonfarm payrolls print — well below the ~110,000 consensus — has kept September rate-hike odds near 50-58%, down from ~66% before the report, cushioning the bond sell-off.

news.head: Microsoft layoffs
news.body: Microsoft announced 4,800 job cuts (2.1% of workforce), including roughly one-fifth of its Xbox division, citing accelerating AI-driven transformation of how software is built and deployed.

news.head: OPEC+ supply increase
news.body: OPEC+ agreed to raise output by 188,000 barrels per day in August — the fifth consecutive monthly increase — as Strait of Hormuz tanker flows partially recover under the interim US-Iran peace agreement.

news.head: Q2 earnings season opens
news.body: PepsiCo reports Thursday before the open (est. EPS ~$2.19) and Delta Air Lines follows Friday, giving the market its first read on consumer spending power and summer travel demand.

implications: Today's FOMC minutes are the binary event: hawkish language confirming the dot-plot's hike bias would lift the 10-year yield further above 4.55% (OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET) and pressure high-multiple tech; a softer tone would validate the post-payrolls rally.

The Hormuz LNG strike is a wildcard — WTI crude (OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET ~$72.16/bbl, up ~2.4%) rising further would add to inflation expectations and keep the Fed cautious, while also boosting energy-sector stocks.

Breadth divergence is constructive: most S&P 500 names rose Tuesday even as the Nasdaq fell, suggesting the bull market is broadening rather than breaking — watch financials, industrials, and energy as rotation beneficiaries.

Positioning: Nasdaq 100 futures speculators are at the 4th percentile of a 3-year range — almost no bullish bets left, a contrarian floor for tech. Russell 2000 futures are at the 2nd percentile — a similarly extended short position with squeeze risk if the FOMC minutes disappoint hawks. VIX futures specs are also near historic lows in net longs, consistent with complacency that any hawkish shock could rapidly unwind. Copper specs are at the 95th percentile — extended long — a contrarian warning given OPEC+ supply increase and China demand uncertainty. British pound futures specs are at the 1st percentile — speculators have almost no bullish bets left — a contrarian floor for sterling.

watch.head: FOMC minutes (2pm ET)
watch.body: Nine dot-plot members project a 2026 hike; any explicit discussion of September as 'live' would be the day's biggest market mover for bonds, the dollar, and growth stocks.

watch.head: EIA crude inventories (9:30am ET)
watch.body: Previous draw was 3.775M barrels; a second consecutive draw, combined with the Hormuz strike, would reinforce the oil bid and inflation concerns.

watch.head: 10-year yield ~4.56%
watch.body: The OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET 10-year yield has already moved ~8 bps above the prior cash close of 4.48%; a clean break above 4.60% would intensify pressure on the CAPE-41.77 equity market.

watch.head: USD/JPY ~162.4
watch.body: The yen (OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET ~162.43/dollar, at 40-year lows and the 99.7th percentile of 3 years) is the most extreme FX reading in the data — Japanese intervention risk is acute and could cause sudden, sharp yen strength.

watch.head: Semiconductors open
watch.body: After a 4.5%+ sector rout Tuesday, watch whether buyers return at the open or whether the AI-valuation debate triggers a second day of selling.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10-year Treasury yield OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET ~4.56%, up from the PRIOR CASH CLOSE of 4.48%, driven by renewed Hormuz-security fears lifting oil and inflation expectations.
2-year Treasury yield PRIOR CASH CLOSE 4.13%; the yield curve (2s10s) was 35 bps at the prior close — still positively sloped, meaning bond markets are not pricing a near-term recession.
Real interest rates stand at 2.3% (PRIOR CASH CLOSE) and the 10-year inflation breakeven is 2.24% — real rates are meaningfully above zero, which is a genuine drag on borrowing and asset prices.

Term premium — the extra yield investors demand to hold long bonds rather than roll short ones — is 73.2 bps (as of Jul 2), near multi-year highs, signalling bond buyers want compensation for uncertainty.
The Fed held rates at 3.50%-3.75% in June; today's FOMC minutes will reveal how many members were genuinely close to voting for a hike and whether September is being discussed.

Financial conditions remain loose: the Chicago Fed's National Financial Conditions Index is -0.49 (as of Jun 26), meaning money is flowing freely despite higher rates — supportive for risk assets unless the minutes shift the narrative.
DXY dollar index OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET ~100.89, roughly flat versus the PRIOR CASH CLOSE of 101.12 — the dollar is not yet breaking out, which limits the headwind to commodities and EM assets.
sections.positioning: Rates: 3M SOFR futures speculators are at the 1st percentile of 3 years — almost no bullish bets left, a contrarian floor suggesting the market has already priced considerable tightening risk into the short end.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500 PRIOR CASH CLOSE 7,503.85; OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET S&P 500 futures ~7,500, essentially flat — the index is digesting Tuesday's chip-led Nasdaq drag with breadth holding up.
Nasdaq 100 PRIOR CASH CLOSE 25,818.69, down ~1.8% on the session; OVERNIGHT/PRE-MARKET Nasdaq futures ~29,400 (continuous contract basis) signal a tentative stabilization.
Dow Jones PRIOR CASH CLOSE 52,925.15, which surrendered Monday's record 53,055.91 close — industrials and value names are the relative safe haven in this rotation.
VIX PRIOR CASH CLOSE 16.13 — still comfortably below the historical average of ~20, indicating no panic, though a burst of unusual options buying in protection could emerge ahead of the FOMC minutes.
67% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day average (PRIOR CASH CLOSE) and 65.1% above their 200-day average — broad market internals remain healthy despite index-level tech weakness.
Shiller CAPE ratio is 41.77 (PRIOR CASH CLOSE), well above long-run averages, meaning equities offer thin margin of safety if the rate narrative turns more hawkish.
The equity risk premium — the extra return stocks offer over bonds — is -2.05%, meaning Treasuries currently appear more attractive than stocks on a pure yield basis, a structural headwind.
SKEW index at 145.7 (PRIOR CASH CLOSE) shows the options market is pricing meaningful tail-risk — investors are quietly paying up for downside protection even as VIX looks calm.
Four major AI hyperscalers raised their collective 2026 capital expenditure budget to $750 billion, supporting the AI infrastructure thesis even as near-term chip valuations face scrutiny.
sections.positioning: Equities: Nasdaq 100 futures speculators are at the 4th percentile (3-year range) — almost no bullish bets left, a contrarian floor. Russell 2000 futures are at the 2nd percentile with shorts heavy at ~3.2% of open interest net long — squeeze risk is elevated if the FOMC minutes are less hawkish than feared. VIX futures specs are at the 12th percentile, also an extended short position, meaning complacency is high.

single_name.note: CarMax (Consumer Cyclical) — company insiders have been buying (2 insider rules fired), large off-exchange block buying (quiet institutional accumulation) detected, a burst of unusual options buying confirmed, shorts are heavy at 4.37 days-to-cover creating squeeze risk, and the stock trades above its 200-day moving average. Fresh signal as of Jul 6.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High-yield vs. investment-grade credit spread is 272 bps (PRIOR CASH CLOSE Jul 6) — not distressed, but worth monitoring given rising Treasury yields.
Investment-grade option-adjusted spread is 75 bps (PRIOR CASH CLOSE Jul 6) — tight, reflecting strong corporate balance sheets and benign default expectations.
The HY/IG ETF ratio at 1.3526 (PRIOR CASH CLOSE) — markets are not pricing a credit event.
Commercial paper funding costs are 21 bps above risk-free (PRIOR CASH CLOSE Jul 3) — short-term corporate borrowing markets are functioning normally.

Bank reserves sit at $2,966.9 billion (as of Jul 1) — ample system liquidity; the Fed's reverse-repo facility has drained to just $4.5 billion (PRIOR CASH CLOSE), confirming excess cash has largely been absorbed.
The Treasury General Account holds $880.2 billion (as of Jul 1), meaning the government has substantial buffer and is not a near-term liquidity drain.
M2 money supply is growing at 5.58% year-over-year (as of May) — still well above the pre-pandemic average, providing a backstop for nominal asset prices.
Bank credit is expanding at 6.33% year-over-year (as of Jun 24) — lending is healthy, consistent with ISM manufacturing at 53.3 (above the 50 expansion threshold) and ISM services at 54.5.
sections.positioning: Credit: Primary-dealer holdings of high-yield bonds are at the 89th percentile of their 3-year range — dealers are extended long, a contrarian warning that the high-yield spread could widen if risk appetite fades on hawkish FOMC minutes.

single_name.note: Matador Resources (Energy) — company insiders have been buying (2 insider rules fired), large off-exchange block buying and a burst of unusual options buying both active, shorts are heavy at 7.64 days-to-cover creating meaningful squeeze risk, trades above its 200-day line. Signal aging at 75% weight remaining — pair with the oil/Hormuz bid today.
